maya: Quick thread — saw ~30% p95 tail regression on dashboards after last spike. digging into traces, authz checks on every tile are showing lots of DB roundtrips. thinking about a perm cache in the query layer. quick takes?
jordan: can you paste the flame/trace link and a sample query?
maya: https://internal.traces/gh12345 — main hotspot is `QueryExecutor -> PermissionsService.check` on tile render fanout. sample: `GET /console/dash/tiles?ids=[..]` -> multiple perm checks per tile.
ash: Cache should help but invalidation is the tricky bit. role/permission updates are infrequent but critical to be correct.
leo: Options imo: TTL-only (short TTL like 30s), pub/sub invalidation (on role update emit event), or hybrid: fast local cache + central invalidation. Also consider caching positives vs negatives differently.
sophie: If we do local in-process LRU per-worker it's cheap reads but cluster-wide invalidation is hard. Redis central cache gives us atomic evict and metrics. tradeoffs on latency vs correctness.
maya: rough pseudocode:
```
# pseudo
def has_access(user, resource):
  entry = redis.hget(user, resource)
  if entry and entry.expires > now: return entry.allowed
  allowed = authz.svc.check(user, resource)
  redis.hset(user, resource, {allowed, expires=now+30s})
  return allowed
```
(just to make the idea concrete)
jordan: don't cache denies for long. recommend tiny TTL for negative responses (e.g., 15s) and longer for allows.
ash: Also need audit trail: when we fall back to real check we should log `fallback=true` and trace id. SLO discussion: if cache lookup fails or central cache is down, do we fail open or closed? for sensitive ops -> fail closed. for non-sensitive dashboard renders -> degrade to cached allow if available, else show placeholder.
leo: Suggest route-level config: `sensitivity: high|low`. high => strict checks (no stale allow), low => can serve stale allow for up to X seconds. This keeps interface boundary simple: QueryAuthz.is_allowed(ctx, resource, sensitivity).
sophie: Telemetry to add before rollout: `cache_hit_ratio`, `cache_miss_count`, `invalidation_events`, `denied_after_cache` (security metric), `stale_allow_served`. Also per-tenant metrics.
maya: Canary/rollout plan idea: enable central redis-perm-cache for internal org only, run 48h with mutation traffic enabled. enforce short TTLs initially (allow=5m? maybe too long — start allow=5m, deny=15s) and watch `denied_after_cache`. rollback if any denied_after_cache>0 for internal org.
dev-bot: deploy scheduled: canary-perm-cache -> staging -> prod (manual promote) :gear:
jordan: one more interface thought: return `(allowed, source)` where `source` in {cache, authz-service, snapshot}` to aid debugging and tracing. Also include a `version` so we can roll forward changes and detect stale logic.
nash: Long-term thought — instead of per-request checks, we could maintain materialized permission snapshots per-tenant (precomputed permission sets) built by an async job. This moves work off the tail-path and simplifies invalidation to snapshot updates. That's a bigger refactor but worth tracking in RFC.
maya: OK i'll write a short RFC with: design options, TTL defaults (start: allow=5m, deny=15s), invalidation via pub/sub + explicit evict API, canary plan, telemetry, and rollback criteria. will include minimal pseudo code and migration checklist.
sophie: +1
leo: +1
jordan: +1 (please add quick mitigation steps if redis is flaky)
maya: noted — mitigation: local fallback cache per-worker (very short) and circuit-breaker to disable caching if redis RTT > 50ms.
sophie: :thumbsup:
